sentences.text: Hdfc Ergo Gen Ins Co Ltd., Hyderabad vs Pericharla Srujana,

Secunderabad And 3 ... on 11 November, 2024
 The Honourable Smt. Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1342 Of 2016
Judgment:

1. Aggrieved by the order passed by the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal -cum- I Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Secunderabad in M.V.O.P.No.303 of 2013, dated 08.09.2015, the 2nd respondent in the said M.V.O.P./Insurance Company preferred the present Appeal seeking to allow the Appeal by setting aside the order of the learned Tribunal.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal -cum- I Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Secunderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter be referred as they were arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the claim petitioners, who are the wife and parents of the deceased-P.Anil Sidhartha, filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- against the Respondent Nos.1 & 2 for the death of the deceased in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 16.06.2012.

It is stated by the petitioners that on 16.06.2012 at 7.30 PM, when the deceased was proceeding on his Hero Honda Motor Cycle bearing No.AP-28BH-1305 from Gandimaisamma Cross roads towards Bachupally on extreme left side with great care and diligence and when reached near Reddy labs, suddenly in the dark night,
the driver of Tractor & Trailer bearing Nos.AP-27F-8528 and AP-27F-8529 stopped the said MGP,J Tractor and Trailer in the middle of the road without any precautions of putting indicators, parking lights, radium stickers, stones, etc. due to which the deceased dashed the said Tractor and Trailer and sustained severe Head injury and died on the spot.
It is stated by the petitioners that the deceased was aged 28 years and was hale and healthy and used to work as Trainee Engineer.

Due to the sudden demise of the deceased, the petitioners suffered mental agony and lost their source of income and hence filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- against the respondent Nos.1 & 2, who are the owner and insurer of the subject Tractor and Trailer bearing Nos.AP-27F-8528 and AP-27F- 8529.
4. Respondent No.1- Owner of the subject Tractor and Trailer, filed his counter denying the averments made in the claim petition including, rash and negligent stationing of the crime vehicle on the middle of the road, injuries sustained to the deceased, death of the deceased due to injuries and contended that as the crime vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 having valid insurance policy, hence, the liability, if any fixed, would be against both the respondents jointly and severally.

5. Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed its counter contending that the vehicle involved in the accident is a commercial vehicle and the person who drove the same do not hold MGP,J valid driving license and the owner of the Tractor violated the terms and conditions of the policy by handing over the subject vehicle to an unqualified driver and that there is no valid permit for the Hdfc Ergo Gen Ins Co Ltd., Hyderabad vs Pericharla Srujana, Secunderabad And 3 ... on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16544670/
1 subject Tractor, as such, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.
6. Based on the pleadings made by both the parties, the learned Tribunal had framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the pleaded accident occurred resulting in death of deceased-P.Ail Sidhartha due to the rash and negligent parking of the Tractor and Trailer bearing No.AP-27F-8528 and AP-27F-8529 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation and if so, at what quantum and what is the liability of the respondents?
3. To what relief?
7. Before the Tribunal, on behalf of the petitioners, PWs1 to 3 were examined and Exs.A1 to A13,
Exs.X1 & X2 were marked.

sentences.text: On behalf of Respondents, RW1 was examined and Exs.B1 to B3 were marked.

8. After considering the evidence and documents available on record, the learned Tribunal allowed the claim petition of the petitioners by awarding compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum payable by both the respondents jointly and severally.

Aggrieved by the same,
the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company preferred the present Appeal.
MGP,J 9.
Heard both sides and perused the material available on record.

10. The contentions of the learned Standing Counsel for appellant/Insurance Company are that as the driver of the subject Tractor and Trailer do not hold valid driving license and valid permit to drive a commercial vehicle i.e., the subject Tractor and Trailer, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation and hence prayed to allow the Appeal by setting aside the order of the learned Tribunal.

11. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents contended that the learned Tribunal,
after considering all the aspects, had awarded reasonable compensation and interference of this Court is unwarranted.
12.
Now the point that emerges for determination is, Whether the order passed by the learned Tribunal requires interference of this Court?
POINT:-
13. As seen from the record, there is no dispute about the occurrence of accident and death of the deceased.

Hence, this Court considers that there is no necessity to once again delve into the above Hdfc Ergo Gen Ins Co Ltd., Hyderabad vs Pericharla Srujana, Secunderabad And 3 ... on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16544670/
2 aspect.

sentences.text: The only point that has to be decided in the present Appeal is whether the Tribunal erred in imposing liability upon the appellant though the driver of the subject Tractor and MGP,J Trailer do not possess valid driving license to drive a commercial vehicle and is not having valid permit at the time of accident.

14. In this regard, it is pertinent to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in the case between National Insurance Co. Ltd Vs.Swaran Singh & Ors 1 wherein, the Hon'ble Court in its Summary of Findings at point Nos.(iii) to (vi) of its judgment, held as under:-
"(iii) The breach of policy condition e.g., disqualification of driver or invalid driving licence of the driver, as contained in sub-section (2)(a)(ii) of Section 149, have to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd Vs.Swaran Singh & Ors 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mere absence, fake or invalid driving licence or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.

To avoid its liability towards insured,
the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

(iv) The insurance companies are, however, with a view to avoid their liability must not only establish the available defence(s) raised in the said proceedings but must also establish 'breach' on the part of the owner of the vehicle; the burden of proof wherefor would be on them.
(v) The court cannot lay down any criteria as to how said burden would be discharged, inasmuch as the same would depend upon the facts and circumstance of each case.

(vi) Even where the insurer is able to prove breach on the part of the insured concerning the policy condition regarding holding of a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant AIR 2004 SUPREME COURT 1531 MGP,J period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards insured unless the said breach or breaches on the condition of driving licence is/ are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.

The Tribunals in interpreting the policy conditions would apply "the rule of main purpose" and the concept of "fundamental breach" to allow defences available to the insured under Section 149(2) of the Act."

15. Therefore, from the above doctrine, it is made clear that even if the insurer is able to prove breach on part of the insured concerning the policy condition regarding holding of a valid license by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards insured unless the said breach or breaches on the condition of driving license is/are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.

It is also pertinent to state that even if the driver possess license for one type of vehicle but found driving another type of vehicle, the fact that the driver not possessing requisite license is not a ground to the insurer to avoid its liability on technical breach of conditions concerning driving license.

Minor breaches of license conditions which are not found to have been direct causes of the accident would be treated as minor breaches or inconsequential deviation in the matter of use of vehicles and they would not constitute sufficient ground to deny the benefit of coverage of insurance to third parties.
It is also pertinent to state that driving of a non-transport vehicle has no difference from driving a MGP,J transport vehicle as there would be no difference in the driving skills.
The absence of endorsement on the license permitting the driver to drive transport variety of vehicle is not a fundamental breach but a technical shortfall on part of the driver of offending tractor.

Hence,
the appellant /Insurance Company cannot be absolved from its liability in paying compensation.
Therefore, this Court do not find any reason to interfere with the findings of the learned Tribunal which are in proper perspective.
Hence, the Appeal is devoid of merits and is liable to be dismissed.
17. In the result, the Appeal is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
18. Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
